analysis.title: Summary from our US Tuesday call with Jay on TJX
key_insights: UBS's Jay Sole is strongly bullish on TJX and treats the Marmaxx slowdown as an execution issue, not a broken thesis. Q2 comps were +4% overall vs +1% at Marmaxx, where a higher basket was offset by fewer transactions.
HomeGoods, Canada and International Q2 comps were +7%, +6% and +7%, which Jay cites as evidence the slowdown is localized to Marmaxx.
Management called the Marmaxx issue self-inflicted and merchandise-mix related. Jay's best explanation is that TJX missed a fashion trend and reacted too slowly.
Jay says comparable episodes occurred roughly four times over 30 years. They typically took 2-3 quarters to correct, and once took 4.

TJX's differentiation per Jay: 21,000+ vendor relationships, substantial direct sourcing, inventory turns of roughly every three weeks, buyers who act like portfolio managers, and the in-store 'treasure hunt'. He sees value + discovery + changing assortment as hard to replicate through e-commerce or agentic AI.

International is a second growth engine versus Ross and Burlington. TJX has 5,214 stores at FY2026 year-end vs a 7,500 long-term target, including 300 additional Marmaxx and 200 additional HomeGoods locations.

Jay does not read Ross's strength mainly as share loss for TJX. He argues Ross and Burlington are taking share from department stores and weaker specialty retailers, and that moderate inflation supports off-price unless it becomes a recession-level shock.

Growth framework: roughly 6-7% annual sales growth, 10-20bps annual margin expansion and buybacks. TJX returned $1.3bn through buybacks and dividends in Q2. The UBS framework is ~11% five-year EPS CAGR, 30x P/E and a $198 PT.
The earnings bridge discussed on the call was about $5.35 EPS in the current year, ~$6 next year, approaching $7 in FY28. ~30x on close-to-$7 implies around $200+ vs approximately $141 at the time.

Catalyst: TJX reports Q3 earnings on November 18. Jay's near-term framework is credit-card trends (Bloomberg TJX → ALTD) feeding reported Marmaxx comps. He expects evidence of Marmaxx recovery around the end of Q4 / Christmas season into January.
Principal risk is that Marmaxx does not recover. Jay thinks investors want comps back toward mid-single digits. Management's Q2 commentary pointed toward a 2-3% comp cadence by Q4.
Q2 merchandise margin partly benefited from tariff refunds whose future amount and timing are uncertain. Management indicated underlying results were ahead even excluding them.

Positioning: Jay describes investor interest in TJX as very high. In a strong risk-on rally TJX could lag more beaten-down or lower-quality names. He sees investors seeking more balance away from AI/Magnificent Seven concentration, not a wholesale rotation.

Jay says investor discussions are moving toward On Holding, Levi's, Ralph Lauren and Tapestry. Positioning in Nike and Lululemon remains notably bearish, and consumer-discretionary crowding has begun to edge higher after declining in the first half of the year.

Jay describes US consumer spending as quite strong, with retail sales growing at a mid-single-digit pace through much of the year. UBS surveys 8,000 US consumers monthly, and Jay reads recent data as a shift toward off-price/value.

market_movers.rationale: Jay Sole is strongly bullish and sees Marmaxx as a temporary execution issue. The $198 PT rests on ~11% five-year EPS CAGR and 30x P/E.
Jay noted bearish UBS views on Macy's as part of his argument that weaker department stores are losing share to off-price. The rating is described only as bearish.
Jay noted bearish UBS views on Kohl's, which still has more than $20bn in revenue and is a source of share for off-price.
Jay noted bearish UBS views on Dillard's as part of the off-price share-gain argument. The rating is described only as bearish.

sector_views.rationale: Jay sees off-price as a structural share-gain story, taking share from department stores and weaker specialty retailers.

sector_views.sector: Department stores and weaker specialty retail
sector_views.rationale: UBS has bearish views on Macy's, Kohl's and Dillard's. Children's Place is cited as an extreme example of pressure, with a market value of roughly $5m vs ~$2bn historically.

earnings_insights: TJX Q3 earnings are scheduled for November 18. Q2 was reported 2026-08-20.
TJX Q2 comps (reported) were +4% overall, Marmaxx +1%, HomeGoods +7%, Canada +6% and International +7%. Marmaxx had a higher basket and fewer transactions.
TJX Q2 segment margins (reported): HomeGoods 12.4%, International 7.3%.
Q2 merchandise margin benefited partly from tariff refunds. Management said underlying results were ahead even excluding them.
TJX returned $1.3bn through buybacks and dividends in Q2 (reported).
Q3 Marmaxx comp is being discussed in low-single-digit territory. Management's Q2 commentary pointed toward a 2-3% comp cadence by Q4.
EPS bridge discussed on the call (UBS estimates, not reported): about $5.35 current year, ~$6 next year, approaching $7 in FY28.
FY2026 revenue (reported) was approximately $60.3bn: roughly $47.1bn US, $5.4bn Canada, $7.2bn Europe and $0.6bn Australia.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Jay described spending as quite strong, with growth stronger in some months. This supports the consumer backdrop for off-price.

trade_ideas.description: Long TJX into Q3 earnings on Nov 18, monitoring credit-card trends via Bloomberg TJX → ALTD for Marmaxx comps
trade_ideas.rationale: Jay sees Marmaxx as a temporary execution issue and expects recovery toward mid-single-digit comps.
trade_ideas.risk: Marmaxx does not recover, the fashion miss proves structural, or a recession-level inflation shock hits the consumer.

risk_factors: Marmaxx comps fail to recover toward mid-single digits.
The fashion miss proves more persistent or structural, with continued weak transactions.
International expansion requires real estate, local talent, sourcing infrastructure and regulatory execution.
A severe inflation shock or recession could overwhelm the value-proposition benefit.
Tariff refunds that helped Q2 merchandise margin are uncertain in amount and timing.
Positioning: high investor interest creates relative-performance risk in a strong risk-on rally.
vol_and_positioning: Jay described investor interest in TJX as very high, so a visible Marmaxx improvement could draw meaningful incremental buying.
Positioning in Nike and Lululemon remained notably bearish, while consumer-discretionary crowding began to edge higher after declining in the first half of the year.
In a strong risk-on rally, TJX could lag relative to more beaten-down or lower-quality names because it is already popular and well-owned.
geopolitical: The election discussion was linked to possible developments involving Iran and oil prices, including a scenario in which oil falls. Part of the answer is missing from the transcript.
cross_bank_references: Jay's framework compares TJX with Ross and Burlington but cites no other bank's view.
UBS holds bearish views on Macy's, Kohl's and Dillard's, and Nordstrom previously carried neutral/sell ratings before going private.

tension_points.bull_case: Marmaxx is a temporary merchandising miss. Comps recover toward mid-single digits as in roughly four prior episodes over 30 years, HomeGoods, Canada and International stay healthy, and the multiple returns to the high-20s/low-30s, supporting the $198 PT.
tension_points.bear_case: Marmaxx does not recover despite corrective actions. Transactions stay weak, buying execution stays challenged, and investors will not restore the historical premium multiple.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Marmaxx comps failing to improve toward mid-single digits, with evidence of recovery expected around the end of Q4 / Christmas season into January.
